security_audit.summary: Static backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown command examples, code fences, and inline CLI names. The skill is transparent about using the `belt` CLI, but its wildcard `Bash(belt *)` permission creates a broader execution surface than the documented workflow needs.

remediation.suggestion: Replace `Bash(belt *)` with the smallest set of `belt` subcommands required for login, image generation, stitching, and app browsing.

remediation.issue: External AI service sends prompt content off device
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear note that storyboard prompts may be sent to inference.sh or model providers, and advise users not to include confidential scripts.

content.user_title: Create Film Storyboards With AI Panels
content.value_statement: Storyboard planning often fails when shot language, continuity, and panel notes are inconsistent. This skill gives structured film guidance and AI panel prompts for clearer pre-production work.
actual_capabilities: Explains common shot types, camera angles, and camera movement terms for storyboard panels.
Provides continuity guidance for the 180-degree rule, match on action, eyeline match, and screen direction.
Defines a panel annotation format with shot, movement, duration, action, dialogue, sound, and music fields.
Shows a step-by-step workflow from shot list to generated panels and stitched storyboard pages.
Includes example `belt` CLI prompts for generating consistent storyboard panel images.
limitations: Requires the external inference.sh `belt` CLI for image generation examples.
Does not guarantee visual character consistency across every generated panel.
Does not replace a director, cinematographer, or production designer review.
Does not include downloadable storyboard templates or project files.

use_cases.title: Plan a Short Film Scene
use_cases.description: Create a shot list, continuity notes, and panel prompts for a compact narrative scene.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Ad Concept Board
use_cases.description: Turn a campaign idea into clear panels with camera framing, action notes, and visual style guidance.

use_cases.title: Prototype an Animation Sequence
use_cases.description: Map action beats, screen direction, and panel annotations before building an animatic.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Storyboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a six-panel storyboard for this scene: [describe scene]. Include shot type, camera angle, action, and dialogue notes for each panel.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Shot List
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this script excerpt into a numbered shot list. Use WS, MS, CU, and ECU labels, and include continuity notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Consistent AI Panels
prompt_templates.prompt: Write AI image prompts for each storyboard panel. Keep character details, aspect ratio, lens style, lighting, and color grade consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Storyboard Continuity
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this storyboard plan for 180-degree rule errors, eyeline mismatches, screen direction issues, and missing annotations. Suggest fixes.

output_examples.input: A character finds an unsigned envelope on her office desk.
output: Panel 1 uses a wide office establishing shot in morning light.
Panel 2 uses a medium shot as she approaches the desk.
Panel 3 uses an extreme close-up of the envelope and handwriting.
Panel 4 uses a close-up reaction shot with a slow dolly in note.

output_examples.input: Review a dialogue storyboard between two people at a table.
output_examples.output: The review flags camera positions that cross the 180-degree line, adds an over-the-shoulder pair, and recommends a neutral cutaway before changing sides.

output_examples.input: Create prompts for a three-panel chase sequence.
output_examples.output: The output keeps the same lens, color grade, and character details while varying wide, tracking, and close-up shots for pacing.

best_practices: Start each scene with a shot list before generating images.
Use one style suffix across panels to maintain visual consistency.
Add annotations for movement, duration, action, dialogue, sound, and music.
anti_patterns: Do not use the same shot size for every panel in a scene.
Do not cross the 180-degree line without a planned transition.
Do not include confidential scripts in external image-generation prompts.

faq.question: Does this skill generate storyboard images directly?
faq.answer: It provides `belt` CLI examples for image generation. Users need the external CLI and related service access.

faq.question: Can it help with shot vocabulary?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common shot sizes, camera angles, movement types, and when to use them.

faq.question: Does it cover continuity rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers the 180-degree rule, match on action, eyeline match, and screen direction.

faq.question: Is it useful for animation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure panels and action beats before building an animatic or animation plan.

faq.question: What tools does it depend on?
faq.answer: The examples depend on the inference.sh `belt` CLI for generating and stitching images.

faq.question: Should users include private scripts?
faq.answer: No. External image generation may send prompts to a service, so users should remove confidential details.
